findings.title: jint_strict silently defaults string/bool/null sim values to the field default (ok=true) — the r1 Float fix is incomplete
findings.detail: Empirically verified: "volume": "high" -> (0, true), "multiplier": true -> (1, true). Only json.Float is rejected; String/Boolean/Null fall through the #partial switch to the silent default — a live silent-default catalog path, contra ODN-5, in the exact helper the r1 fix introduced.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a default case to jint_strict returning (0, false) for any non-Integer value (String/Boolean/Null/Object/Array); add string/bool negative rows to the fail-fast table.

findings.title: jint_strict narrows i64 json.Integer to i32 BEFORE any range check — 2^32-scale values wrap into valid small values
findings.detail: Empirically verified: "era": 4294967297 -> (1, true) passes the era 1..64 check; 4294967296 -> 0. Same wrap family as the r1 default_lane u8 finding (fixed pre-cast at the lane sites) but now inside jint_strict itself, so EVERY new 3.1 field is wrappable. ODN-5 fail-fast bar bypassed.
findings.recommended_fix: In jint_strict's Integer branch, check x within i32 range before the cast (x < -2^31 || x > 2^31-1 -> return 0, false); add 2^32-era/volume test rows.

findings.title: node_types demand_weight fail-fast rules (integer-only + >= 0) have NO negative rows — the only 3.1 rules in the diff without coverage
findings.evidence: catalog_test.odin uses NT_VALID as a fixed baseline (3 occurrences); zero node_types negative rows. The two new rules: 'if !okd { return ... demand_weight must be an integer }' and 'if nt.demand_weight < 0 { return ... }'.

findings.title: Wrong-typed per-era entries/set_pieces KEYS silently accepted as 'no entries' — soft-check inconsistent with the hard eras/packet_types checks
findings.evidence: if es, okes := eo["entries"].(json.Array); okes { ... } / if sps, oksps := eo["set_pieces"].(json.Array); oksps {
findings.detail: "entries": {} (present but wrong type) silently loads an era with zero demand, while the same block hard-rejects a bad eras key and packet_types hard-rejects bad entries. Silent-empty on malformed JSON, contra ODN-5. (The or_continue row-skip is the r1-rejected house pattern — NOT re-opened.)
findings.recommended_fix: Mirror the eras check: if the key is present but not an array, return a named error ('entries must be an array').

findings.title: catalogs_load never json.destroy's its parse trees — the new 43-row fail-fast suite surfaces ~5,000 leaked allocations in `odin test core`
findings.evidence: odin test core: 5028 leak lines, e.g. '+++ leak 1.56KiB [parser.odin:299:parse_object_body()]' + '+++ leak ... [catalog.odin:251:catalogs_load()]'
findings.detail: Every catalogs_load call (46 in the suite, plus app/harness) leaks the parsed JSON tree. Pattern pre-exists in the 1.2 loaders but was silent (no tests called catalogs_load); the new suite makes it loud in the gate output. Bounded one-shot, no sim impact.
findings.recommended_fix: json.destroy_value(v) on each parse tree's exit path in catalogs_load (or parse into a scratch allocator); clears the gate noise.

findings.title: effective_volume i32 multiply can wrap for accepted large multipliers — set-piece multiplier has no upper bound
findings.evidence: v *= sp.multiplier  (loader check: 'if mult < 1 || st < 0 || dt < 1 || fl < 0' — lower bound only)
findings.detail: multiplier 2^30 x volume 2 wraps i32 negative -> vol <= 0 silently skips the class all window; huge positive values -> OOM. Only reachable with absurd-but-accepted catalog data; ODN-5 upper-bound gap in the new loader.
findings.recommended_fix: Bound multiplier at load (e.g. reject > 1000) or compute effective_volume in u64 with an overflow guard.

findings.title: Flow-level dst-distribution pin exercises only UNIFORM sink weights — the node demand_weight -> weighted_pick wiring is never flow-tested non-uniform
findings.evidence: // qa_fixture — the §3.3 topology: residentials at node ids 0, 1, 3 (all / // demand_weight 1) ... '// §3.3: the dst distribution matches the sink demand_weights (all 1 -> / // uniform over the 3 residentials'
findings.detail: A wiring bug that ignored the catalog weight (always 1) would pass every flow-level test; the non-uniform path is pinned only at the weighted_pick unit level. The collect_terminals->catalog demand_weight link is the untested seam.
findings.recommended_fix: Give one qa_fixture residential demand_weight 3 and assert the flow-level histogram follows 1:3 (+-3-sigma) in test_director_spawns_by_spec.

findings.title: catalogs_hash_sources fold has no unit pin — a dropped source in the fold would pass every gate silently
findings.evidence: TEST_CATALOG_HASH :: u64(0x0123456789ABCDEF) — the unit tests pin the primitive, not the fold; the fold is exercised only via goldens (bless+replay, self-consistent).
findings.detail: If the fold dropped a source, bless+replay would stay internally consistent and the era-3 golden would still pass — the ODN-11 binding for the new catalogs is unpinned at unit level.
findings.recommended_fix: Pin the fold: assert catalogs_hash_sources changes when packet_types/demand bytes differ and stays stable for cosmetic-only changes.
